name: Ceramics Glossary
summary: Grouped ceramics terms whose definitions compose canonical Accordion disclosures and whose related destinations compose canonical Link, without implying unresolved alphabet navigation, filtering, or search behavior.

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.description: Contained glossary presentation; it is labelled by the optional title when one is supplied.

anatomy.name: group
anatomy.description: Repeatable letter group emitted in source order.

anatomy.name: letter
anatomy.description: Contextual heading naming one term group.

anatomy.name: terms
anatomy.description: Canonical Accordion root containing the terms for one group.

anatomy.name: term
anatomy.description: One canonical Accordion item containing a dfn term and definition content.

anatomy.name: termImage
anatomy.description: Optional informative media within a definition.

anatomy.name: relatedLink
anatomy.description: Canonical Link to a real target-owned related destination.

variants.name: default
variants.description: Grouped disclosure glossary without alphabet controls.

sizes.name: default
sizes.description: Fluid contained glossary with no viewport-specific size API.

states.name: default
states.description: Default glossary with the target-selected initial expansion state.

states.name: collapsedTerm
states.description: Collapsed canonical Accordion term with its definition removed from rendering and focus order.

states.name: expandedTerm
states.description: Expanded canonical Accordion term exposing its definition.

behavior.name: glossaryContent
behavior.description: Targets own records, normalized grouping keys, ordering, stable ids, definitions, media, and related destinations; the contract does not define a CMS schema.

behavior.name: canonicalAccordionComposition
behavior.description: Every term consumes canonical Accordion anatomy and behavior rather than recreating disclosure markup, state, focus, or motion.

behavior.name: termSemantics
behavior.description: The visible term uses dfn inside the contextual Accordion heading; the associated panel owns the definition content.

behavior.name: groupPolicy
behavior.description: A target may allow single or multiple expanded terms and may choose the initial expansion state; this component does not add a second controlled or uncontrolled API over Accordion.

behavior.name: titleOmission
behavior.description: When title is omitted, the root also omits the dangling aria-labelledby relationship while grouped headings preserve content structure.

behavior.name: relatedLinks
behavior.description: Related terms compose canonical Link with real target-owned destinations; placeholder or prevented links are not part of the contract.

behavior.name: contentResilience
behavior.description: Long, empty, localized, and bidirectional content wraps in source order without clipping or viewport-specific behavior.

behavior.name: alphabetControlsExcluded
behavior.description: Alphabet navigation, filtering, search, URL state, and result announcements remain outside the v1 API until their product behavior is explicitly decided.

properties.name: terms
properties.description: Target-supplied letter groups and canonical Accordion term items with required terms and definitions plus optional media and related Links.

accessibility: Use contextual native headings for the glossary title, letter groups, and canonical Accordion triggers.
Keep each trigger id, aria-expanded, aria-controls, panel id, optional region label, and native hidden state synchronized through Accordion.
Preserve native Button click, Enter, Space, and normal Tab order; do not add arrow-key behavior to independent disclosure triggers.
Use labelled regions only while the number of simultaneously visible panels remains small enough to avoid landmark proliferation.
Use dfn for the term, informative alternative text for meaningful media, and canonical Links with real destinations for related terms.
Keep long and localized terms readable at 200 percent zoom, in narrow containers, and in right-to-left direction.
Do not introduce alphabet controls until their navigation, filtering, search, URL, focus, and announcement behavior is defined.

web.notes: Ceramics CSS owns grouping and content presentation while canonical Accordion owns disclosure behavior and canonical Link owns related destinations.

shopify.notes: Liquid maps records and groups to canonical Accordion markup or a semantics-preserving details/summary equivalent; the target owns ids and group policy.
